title: Embedding Learning for Fine-grained Segmentation
summary: Factorized class representations into a shared proxy and intra-class variation vectors to reduce boundary confusion between similar classes - validated on 3 datasets and 6 backbones with no extra inference cost.
brief: Model-agnostic embedding factorization with variation-aware proxies for fine-grained segmentation.
overview:
[Members] 1

[Period] Feb 2025 - Jul 2025

[Method Design]
Analyzed the limitations of single-proxy representations and designed a factorized similarity computation combining a representative proxy and variation vectors, with contrastive pull/push losses focused on boundary regions via hard negative selection and focal modulation - improving boundary quality at no additional parameter or inference cost.

[Experiments & Results]
Validated consistent mIoU gains across 6 backbones (HRNet, DeepLabV3, MobileNetV3, PIDNet, SegNeXt, SegFormer) and 3 datasets with distinct scene characteristics (Cityscapes, COCO-Stuff, iSAID), including MobileNetV3+Cityscapes 69.5->72.3. Cross-checked the gains with mask visualization and t-SNE analysis.

[Outcomes]
Published as a first-author SCI journal paper (Neurocomputing, 2025) and filed a domestic patent (Jul 2025).

title: Real-time LWIR Segmentation for Firefighter Navigation
summary: Built and expanded an LWIR dataset and designed a noise-aware segmentation framework with noise suppression and boundary enhancement - achieving prediction stability and real-time speed at once for firefighter navigation.
brief: Noise-robust real-time LWIR segmentation for firefighter navigation with thermal style augmentation.
overview:
[Members] 2

[Period] Mar 2023 - Feb 2025

[Dataset Construction]
Personally established QC criteria and labeling rules for collected data and led repeated review cycles to reduce label quality variance - building KERInha, a synthetic LWIR dataset of 2,495 indoor images (960x600) targeting floor/door classes.

[Data Diversity]
Designed and applied I2I-based LWIR-style augmentation to reduce location bias, identified its structural limitations firsthand, and proposed the direction for transitioning to diffusion-based methods - recognized with a student paper award (IEIE, Jun 2023).

[Framework Design]
Independently designed SDM (stripe noise suppression), BEM (boundary enhancement), and MSFM (local-global feature fusion) on a real-time multi-branch baseline, keeping the total added latency around 16ms.

[Results]
On KERInha, achieved mIoU 67.21 (+6.13 over FTNet, the LWIR-specific SOTA) at 61.2 FPS (~9.4x faster); on the public SODA benchmark, reached mIoU 63.81 with the best class-wise IoU in 19 of 21 classes. Published as a first-author SCI journal paper (IEEE Access, 2025) and filed a domestic patent (Nov 2024).

title: Autolabeling LWIR Images
summary: Built a SAM-based auto-labeling pipeline with verification and retry loops at each stage - generating label maps for 1,820 LWIR images and relieving the initial dataset bottleneck of the main LWIR project.
brief: Text-prompt-based auto-labeling pipeline for LWIR semantic segmentation using Grounding DINO and SAM.
overview:
[Members] 1

[Period] Apr 2023 - Jun 2023

[Pipeline Design]
Using Grounding DINO and SAM as the baseline, restructured the workflow into a multi-stage pipeline: class-wise detection -> instance segmentation -> instance refinement -> mask fusion. Applied text-prompt-based class definition for consistency, and inserted verification and feedback loops that detect failure types (missed detection, unstable masks, over-suppression, pixel conflicts) at each stage and retry or handle exceptions.

[Quality Verification]
Hand-labeled a 200-image random sample to validate the generated labels (~94% pixel accuracy), analyzed the dominant failure conditions (heavy noise, low thermal contrast), and introduced a full overlay-based screening step so that only approved label maps enter the training set.

[Results]
Generated label maps for 1,820 LWIR images, relieving the initial dataset bottleneck of the main LWIR project, with the pipeline designed for reuse on newly collected data.

title: Multimodal Shoe Search with CLIP (FiYS)
summary: Designed a frozen-CLIP retrieval system that combines a reference shoe image with text conditions - recommending shoes that reflect both the intended style and detailed attributes, with improved classification accuracy across all features.
brief: Multimodal retrieval with frozen CLIP and CoOp-based context tuning for accurate shoe search.
overview:
[Members] 3

[Period] Aug 2022 - Dec 2022

[Dataset Construction]
Contributed to building a custom dataset of ~6,000 shoe images labeled with 5 attributes (6 brands, 20 colors, hightop/lowtop, 8 sole types, 97 model names). Defined the attribute information to be stored per image and established exclusion criteria - including cropped, unidentifiable, and low-quality samples - to set the data quality standard for the project.

[System Design]
Kept CLIP (ViT-B/32) frozen and designed a two-stage retrieval flow: identify the reference shoe from the input image via attribute-wise classification, then modify its metadata with the user's text condition and re-search to recommend a shoe reflecting both inputs.

[Prompt Learning]
The attribute classification engine initially relied on hand-crafted prompt ensembles, whose accuracy fluctuated with template composition. Replaced them with learnable context vectors via CoOp - keeping the CLIP encoders frozen - and verified its effect.

[Results]
Top-1/Top-5 classification accuracy improved across all 5 attributes over the prompt ensemble baseline, with the largest gains in attributes hard to describe in language (Sole 14.71 -> 99.25, Name 44.48 -> 93.19, Color 59.23 -> 95.00 in Top-1).
